summary: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, earning a PhD from Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha. He held posts at Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist who earned an MA and PhD from Andhra University and a linguistics diploma from Osmania University. He became Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1971 and held visiting professorships at Chicago and Emory.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University from 2003 to 2008 and was president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies from circa 2006 to 2018.

Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Bhante Dhammasakkaro and earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held positions at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, and King's College London before becoming George A. Saden Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale in 2006.

Verrier Elwin (1902–1964) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Dean Close School and Merton College. From circa 1946 to 1949, he served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India.

Vesna Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at Oxford until 2010 and served as a professor at UC Santa Barbara.

Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA from Yale and a PhD from SOAS University of London. In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago. He founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education and served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. In 2007, he was an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor H. Mair is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard, later teaching at Harvard and joining the University of Pennsylvania faculty in 1979.

Victor Henry (1850–1907) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Douai, University of Lille, and École Centrale de Lille, and became professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at Paris in 1888.

Victor Turner (1920–1983) was a scholar of religious studies who earned degrees from UCL and Manchester. He held academic posts at Manchester, Cornell, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia.
Victoria Sujata is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Michael Aris.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya (1878–1954) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a pandit and Principal at Visva-Bharati University and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who earned her PhD from Cambridge. She has held posts at the Smithsonian Institution, the University of Hong Kong, and Columbia University, where she became Barbara Stoler Miller Professor in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra (1926–2005) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya at Allahabad. He was Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Vijaya Indra Suri was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who founded the Prakrit Text Society and succeeded Vijayadharma Suri, as attested in 1933.

Vilhelm Thomsen (1842–1927) was a Danish linguist who completed his PhD at the University of Copenhagen. He taught there as Privatdozent and associate professor before serving as Professor of comparative linguistics from 1887 to 1913.

Vimla Karnatak is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar. As attested in 2000, she served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University.
